SYN-001.name: Aarav Mehta
SYN-001.urgency_trigger: Hospital Discharge Alert: St. Jude Medical Ctr (14h ago) • 48h TOC Window
SYN-001.sdoh: Lives with daughter • No independent vehicle • Low physical activity
SYN-001.summary: Admitted 2026-10-31 for acute heart failure exacerbation; discharged 2026-11-04. Hospital prescribed Furosemide 40mg daily and Carvedilol 6.25mg BID. No paid claim found for Furosemide in PBM feed. 47-day medical claims lag hides recent inpatient event. Duplicate EV-771 discharge alert received.

imperfections.detail: Medical claims feed lag is 47 days; recent admission missing from claims.
Absence of furosemide paid claim does not confirm non-pickup (could be discount card or 90d sample).
Duplicate ADT discharge event EV-771 arrived 2 mins after original.

SYN-001.monday_action: Verify medication access (Furosemide), reconcile discharge drugs, confirm daughter's availability, and coordinate 7-day PCP visit with transport.

medications.conflict: Prescribed at hospital; no retail fill in PBM. Abandonment or sample risk.
medications.recommendation: Confirm whether pharmacy dispensed or patient has supply

medications.conflict: Omitted from hospital discharge summary. Risk of double ACE/ARB if restarted.

talking_points: 1. Confirm Aarav arrived home safely and check for breathing difficulty / leg swelling.
2. Clarify status of Furosemide water pill: did daughter pick it up or receive hospital samples?
3. Reconcile Lisinopril: confirm it is discontinued to prevent hypotension.
4. Book follow-up visit with Dr. Ramesh Iyer within 7 days; offer plan medical transport voucher.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: Namaste Priya, this is Maria Gonzalez, registered nurse from Medicare Advantage Care Management calling regarding your father Aarav.

transcript.speaker: Priya (Daughter)
transcript.text: Namaste Maria. Yes, my father came home yesterday afternoon. He is resting in bed.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: I see he was prescribed Furosemide for fluid buildup. Did you get a chance to fill that at the pharmacy?

transcript.speaker: Priya (Daughter)
transcript.text: The hospital pharmacy gave us a 3-day starter blister pack before leaving! But we need to refill the full 30-day bottle at CVS tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: That is wonderful! So he has not missed any doses today. Make sure he does not take his old Lisinopril pill anymore.

SYN-002.name: Nisha Patel
SYN-002.urgency_trigger: HbA1c jumped to 9.1% • Reversed Pharmacy Claim on Metformin • Repeat ED visits
SYN-002.sdoh: Works retail shifts • Food insecurity / high-carb diet • Rx affordability stress
SYN-002.summary: Rising risk diabetic with HbA1c deteriorating to 9.1%. Pharmacy feed shows a reversed claim for Metformin 1000mg last month. Medical claims show ED visit for hyperglycemic dizziness 2 weeks ago, but diagnosis code was delayed.

imperfections.detail: Pharmacy fill was entered then reversed 2 hours later at retail (abandoned due to cost).
EHR lists Glipizide 10mg; claims show Glimepiride 4mg; duplicate sulfonylurea risk.
ED visit occurred 18 days ago, claim billed only 3 days ago.

SYN-002.monday_action: Confirm actual medication intake, explore insulin/metformin cost barriers, verify evening availability, coordinate PCP medication alignment.

medications.conflict: Claim reversed at counter ($75 copay tier). Patient went without refill.
medications.recommendation: Switch to generic Tier-1 or dispatch $0 copay card

medications.conflict: EHR lists Glipizide 10mg instead. Dangerous dual-sulfonylurea confusion.
medications.recommendation: Clinician override: clarify active prescription with Dr. Miller

talking_points: 1. Inquire gently about Metformin refill without sounding accusatory.
2. Offer generic $4/month retail option or manufacturer co-pay card.
3. Clarify whether taking Glipizide or Glimepiride to prevent hypoglycemic crashes.
4. Coordinate diabetes educator call during her preferred evening window.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: Hello Nisha, this is Maria from your health plan. I am calling to check in on your diabetes medications and lab numbers.

transcript.speaker: Nisha
transcript.text: Hello Maria. Yes, I've had some trouble. The pharmacy said my copay on Metformin ER went up to $65 this month so I didn't take it home.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: I am so glad you told me. That medication is available in immediate release for $4 at Walmart or through our mail order for $0.

transcript.speaker: Nisha
transcript.text: Really? Nobody explained that to me at the counter. That would help so much with my monthly expenses.

SYN-003.name: Rohan Das
SYN-003.urgency_trigger: 3 ED Visits in 45 Days • Disconnected Primary Phone • No Established PCP Linkage
SYN-003.pcp: Unassigned / Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC) recommended
SYN-003.contact_person: Shelter Case Worker / Alternate Contact on file
SYN-003.sdoh: Transitional housing • No transport • Uninsured dental / chronic pain
SYN-003.summary: 46-year-old Medicaid recipient with 3 recent ED presentations for acute dental pain and abdominal discomfort. Registered primary phone is disconnected. Claim records contain duplicate billing for ED facility fees. Prior care plan stale.

imperfections.detail: Primary phone on file returns operator disconnect message; alternate number is 14 months stale.
Duplicate CPT-99284 emergency room claim submitted under two provider NPIs.
Previous case manager note is over 18 months old with outdated emergency contact.

SYN-003.monday_action: Validate alternate contact via recent hospital encounter face sheet; route to Community Health Worker for in-person outreach; link to dental/FQHC.

medications.conflict: High GI bleeding risk with repeated ED usage.

talking_points: 1. Cross-reference recent hospital registration face sheet for newly entered temporary contact.
2. If unreachable, trigger Community Health Worker (CHW) field outreach at transitional housing center.
3. Coordinate dental benefit authorization to resolve root cause of repeat emergency visits.

transcript.speaker: System
transcript.text: Outdialing primary contact (555) 991-0023... [Three tone disconnect sound]

transcript.speaker: Automated Operator
transcript.text: 'The number you have dialed is no longer in service. Please check the number and dial again.'

transcript.speaker: HiLabs Copilot
transcript.text: Alternative contact discovered in St. Jude ED Face Sheet (dated 4 days ago): Case Worker Anita at Hope Community Shelter (555) 441-2991.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: 1-click redirecting call to Shelter Case Worker Anita...

SYN-004.name: Sana Khan
SYN-004.urgency_trigger: Behavioral Health ED Crisis (72h ago) • Housing Eviction Notice • Stale SDOH Survey
SYN-004.sdoh: Severe housing insecurity (eviction pending) • Food desert • Single mother
SYN-004.summary: 34-year-old mother presenting to psychiatric emergency for panic episode triggered by eviction notice. Conflicting psychotropic medication regimens between inpatient discharge and outpatient pharmacy. SDOH survey is 10 months stale.

imperfections.detail: Discharge list shows Sertraline 50mg + Hydroxyzine 25mg; pharmacy claims show Fluoxetine 20mg filled 6 weeks ago.
Crisis stabilization fee claim delayed by 3 weeks.
Housing status marked 'stable' in last year's survey; contradicted by recent crisis intake note.

SYN-004.monday_action: Use consented SMS channel for gentle engagement; verify psychiatric med transition; connect immediately with housing navigator and food pantry.

medications.conflict: Replaced Fluoxetine; risk of serotonin syndrome if both taken simultaneously.

talking_points: 1. Greet with trauma-informed, empathetic tone; honor privacy preferences.
2. Confirm she discontinued Fluoxetine before starting Sertraline.
3. Connect directly with health plan Housing Assistance Coordinator to stay eviction.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: Hi Sana, this is Maria, nurse case manager with your health plan. I wanted to see how you are feeling and help with your housing and health resources.

transcript.speaker: Sana
transcript.text: Hi Maria. It is a bit hectic right now with the kids. I got the new medicine from the hospital, but I was scared to take it with my old pills.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: You made the right choice to pause and ask! You should stop the old Prozac completely. The new Sertraline replaces it.

SYN-005.name: Meera Joshi
SYN-005.urgency_trigger: Fall with Hip Contusion • Home Health Referral Status Unknown • Son Caregiver Exhaustion
SYN-005.sdoh: High fall risk home environment • Caregiver burnout • Cognitive slowing
SYN-005.summary: 79-year-old dual-eligible member discharged post-fall with severe hip contusion. Home health physical therapy referral status missing in feeds. Feeds show two duplicate member IDs across Medicaid and Medicare databases. Son requested calls after 6 PM.

imperfections.detail: Medicare ID #M-99120 and State Medicaid ID #MED-4418 not reconciled in old system.
Hospital ordered skilled nursing / physical therapy; authorization feed shows no active request.
Hospital added Gabapentin for nerve pain; prior record flagged high fall risk on sedatives.

SYN-005.monday_action: Reconcile duplicate IDs into single master patient index; escalate missing home health authorization; call son Vikram after 6 PM to evaluate caregiver respite support.

medications.conflict: Beers Criteria warning: High fall risk in 79yo senior with prior fall history.
medications.recommendation: Review safety with Dr. Chen; recommend physical therapy first

medications.conflict: Check for peripheral edema exacerbating mobility.

talking_points: 1. Schedule outreach for 6:15 PM per son's explicit instructions.
2. Expedite Home Health physical therapy authorization with utilization management.
3. Assess caregiver strain: offer plan-funded 20 hours/month respite care benefit.

transcript.speaker: System
transcript.text: Outreach scheduled for 6:15 PM (Son Vikram's preferred window).

transcript.speaker: Vikram (Son - 6:18 PM)
transcript.text: Thank you for calling in the evening Maria. I've been so stressed trying to balance work while making sure mom doesn't fall getting to the bathroom.

transcript.speaker: Maria (RN)
transcript.text: Vikram, you are doing an amazing job, but you do not have to carry this alone. I just pushed through the approval for a Physical Therapist to visit tomorrow, and your plan provides 20 hours of monthly in-home respite support.
